idiom_name: ScalaPB-generated *Grpc service trait with Future-returning stubs
implementation_notes: The ScalaPB gRPC plugin generates an object (for example GreeterGrpc) containing a base trait that declares each RPC - def sayHello(request: HelloRequest): Future[HelloReply] - plus a blocking stub and an asynchronous stub; the facade implements that trait, returns Future (or an effect/stream type through ZIO gRPC, fs2-grpc, Akka gRPC or Pekko gRPC) and delegates to the service layer, with generated case classes as the transfer objects. The effect-system wrappers replace the Future-based stubs but keep the same generated contract, so the choice between them is about the effect type, not about the pattern. A hand-written facade with case-class payloads is justified only for a fixed third-party protocol.
pitfalls: Blocking stubs park the calling thread and can deadlock an effect/Future runtime when invoked inside a callback; prefer the Future- or effect-typed stub.
Failures arrive as StatusRuntimeException rather than as domain errors; translate them into the application's error ADT at the facade boundary.
Generated case classes are the payload: do not pass domain entities with invariants into them, and evolve the .proto rather than editing generated types.
